rows: Quarter size hail covered the ground on the Concho and Menard county line.
The tornado was a brief touch down that was observed by a storm chaser and a local volunteer fire fighter.
Nickel size hail fell from 9:15 to 9:20 P.M.
Wind driven golfball size hail broke about 20 panes of glass at the hospital in Eden. The wind driven golfball size hail also broke windows in homes and vehicles.
Strong thunderstorm winds tore off the roof of a large barn. The strong winds also caused golfball size hail to break windows.
Hail larger than baseballs of about 3.5 inches was measured on the east side of Eden. This wind driven hail storm damaged and destroyed many buildings across Eden.
Golfball size hail was reported just southwest of the intersection of U.S. Highway 83 and Ranch Road 765.
The large hail shattered four windows, the siding and the roof of a mobile home. The hail also broke all of the windows on a truck.
Larger than baseball size hail fell along Ranch Road 765.
A wind gust of near 69 mph was reported.
A rain wrapped tornado was reported approximately 5 miles east northeast of Paint Rock on Farm to Market Road 1929.
An amateur radio operator estimated 60 MPH winds.
Nickel to baseball size hail was reported near the Rural Road 1929 bridge.
A trained storm spotter in the Millersview area observed this tornado 40 to 50 yards east of his location. The tornado remained in open fields and briefly touched down.
Law enforcement reported several road signs blown over in the Millersview area.
The public reported broken skylights and snapped 1 to 2 inch pecan limbs.
A law enforcement official reported an estimated wind gust to 60 MPH.

Baseball size hail was reported by a trained spotter near Paint Rock.

The Eden Volunteer Fire Department reported that thunderstorm winds had removed half of the roof of a barn and knocked down power lines and tree limbs about half a mile southeast of Live Oak. Winds were estimated at 75 mph.
A trained spotter estimated a wind gust near 60 mph at Live Oak.

A storm chaser reported and videotaped this cone tornado. A large dust whirl estimated about 250 yards wide could be seen at the base. It was on the ground for at least two minutes, it moved very little and remained in open country.
